title: Pomerado (YC F26)
summary: Turn any website into an MCP for agents

extra.author: alanjm23
extra.original_title: Launch HN: Pomerado (YC F26) – Turn any website into an MCP for agents

story_text.value:
Hi HN, we’re Alan and Akshay from Pomerado (https://pomerado.ai/). We connect your agents to any website by turning sites into deterministic, self-healing APIs in minutes, fully self-serve.

Agents are no longer limited by their intelligence, but rather by their ability to interact with systems. Airlines, banks, e-commerce, insurance portals, government sites, and legacy portals all lack APIs or MCPs and are common parts of personal assistant or business workflows. Agents instead rely on browser automation or computer use, which can be slow, expensive, and unreliable. And even if computer use were perfect, most companies have banned it out of security and compliance concerns.

We discovered this problem while tinkering with our own personal assistants. When OpenClaw came out, we wanted to “live our lives through our agents” and have them do everything for us. We soon found their usefulness was restricted by what tools they could connect to. For example, when trying to book flights, they fell back on computer use, which failed to checkout. These issues got magnified on repeated workflows, like searching many airlines at once.

Pomerado started off as a project to improve these personal assistant workflows. As we started building, we realized that just-in-time tool creation could have significant applications for AI builders in legacy verticals.

We’re ex-McKinsey and Scale AI, where we drove agent deployments in healthcare, professional services, and telecom. Each time, the biggest bottleneck was getting agents to interface well with legacy websites and apps.

Pomerado is what we built. It’s a self-serve platform where devs can create APIs for any website (even those they don’t own), in minutes. Users (or their coding agents) provide a short natural language description, answer a few questions about their workflow, and receive a MCP in less than an hour. Future tool calls use the deterministic MCP, which usually returns results in 5-30 seconds.

Here’s a walkthrough of our product: https://youtu.be/Bi4jci7rgHo

In practice:

- Our agent opens a browser, explores the website, and performs the requested task once by writing HTTP requests or a Playwright script. This example run establishes how to navigate the website, interact with the relevant controls, and obtain the desired result. If any additional user input is needed (e.g., login, clarification) the agent will ask the user over MCP.

- Afterwards, the agent uses the example run, along with all of the data it recorded, to create a generalizable and repeatable API. Throughout this process, a separate Guardian model reviews the coding agent’s calls against a set of guardrails. We also run a battery of tests with synthetic inputs to ensure that the API is generalized and not overfit to one input. A final publication agent ensures that the integration publishes a reasonable and generalized input/output schema

- We also handle sites that require authentication and 2FA. For authentication, we pass off to a deterministic sign-in process to ensure the model and our recorders never read customer credentials. Users can store 2FA TOTP seeds or link their account to a Pomerado phone number for us to autofill 2FA for them as well

- If future runs fail, a maintenance job is kicked off to repair and improve the tool. The maintenance job can fix broken steps (e.g., a renamed button), add additional functionality (e.g., searching for business class flights in addition to economy), or add new guardrails (e.g., reservation dates must be in the future). We’ve even seen people improve tools by just saying “please make this faster”

Unlike computer use, our MCPs are deterministic at runtime, which makes them much faster and cheaper. By taking slightly longer to do a task the first time, you reap the benefits much more in the future. It’s a great fit for repeated, high-volume tasks you want your agent to do.

We’d love to have you try it! We have both an open-source (MIT) (https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado) and a free hosted version (https://app.pomerado.ai).

So far, users of Pomerado include:

- A personal trainer using agents to prepare workouts and message clients. Before Pomerado, agents couldn’t login and use the site reliably, so this was all manual

- Car dealerships connecting their Grok Bots to legacy dealer systems, including marketplaces, CRMs, and ERPs. Dealers switched from computer use, which could take 1hr+

- Personal assistants using Pomerado to integrate with a broad range of consumer websites

Please ask any questions or share any feedback in the comments, thanks!

Here’s a walkthrough of our product: https://youtu.be/Bi4jci7rgHo

In practice:

- Our agent opens a browser, explores the website, and performs the requested task once by writing HTTP requests or a Playwright script. This example run establishes how to navigate the website, interact with the relevant controls, and obtain the desired result. If any additional user input is needed (e.g., login, clarification) the agent will ask the user over MCP.

- Afterwards, the agent uses the example run, along with all of the data it recorded, to create a generalizable and repeatable API. Throughout this process, a separate Guardian model reviews the coding agent’s calls against a set of guardrails. We also run a battery of tests with synthetic inputs to ensure that the API is generalized and not overfit to one input. A final publication agent ensures that the integration publishes a reasonable and generalized input/output schema

- We also handle sites that require authentication and 2FA. For authentication, we pass off to a deterministic sign-in process to ensure the model and our recorders never read customer credentials. Users can store 2FA TOTP seeds or link their account to a Pomerado phone number for us to autofill 2FA for them as well

- If future runs fail, a maintenance job is kicked off to repair and improve the tool. The maintenance job can fix broken steps (e.g., a renamed button), add additional functionality (e.g., searching for business class flights in addition to economy), or add new guardrails (e.g., reservation dates must be in the future). We’ve even seen people improve tools by just saying “please make this faster”

Unlike computer use, our MCPs are deterministic at runtime, which makes them much faster and cheaper. By taking slightly longer to do a task the first time, you reap the benefits much more in the future. It’s a great fit for repeated, high-volume tasks you want your agent to do.

We’d love to have you try it! We have both an open-source (MIT) (https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado) and a free hosted version (https://app.pomerado.ai).

So far, users of Pomerado include:

- A personal trainer using agents to prepare workouts and message clients. Before Pomerado, agents couldn’t login and use the site reliably, so this was all manual

- Car dealerships connecting their Grok Bots to legacy dealer systems, including marketplaces, CRMs, and ERPs. Dealers switched from computer use, which could take 1hr+

- Personal assistants using Pomerado to integrate with a broad range of consumer websites

Please ask any questions or share any feedback in the comments, thanks!

Building the physical infrastructure that supports Meta technologies takes significant quantities of foundation materials: cement, steel, plastics, and the freight networks that move them. Reducing the emissions associated with building infrastructure requires not only sourcing differently but bringing lower carbon materials and services into existence at commercial scale. Our multi-year commitments give suppliers the revenue certainty they need to build these solutions, and stepping in early helps demonstrate these technologies so the broader market can adopt them. These agreements build on a track record of testing, validating, and scaling lower carbon infrastructure solutions across our data center footprint. Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
summary: Today, Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is publicly available and can be accessed through an AWS Deep Learning Container, released by RadixArk in collaboration with Annapurna Labs. With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you use today. Trainium is a portfolio of AWS AI chips that delivers strong economics for AI training and inference at scale. Now, running SGLang on Trainium follows the SGLang workflow you already know: you launch models through SGLang’s server interface and invoke the endpoint using the same generation APIs. Underneath that interface, SGLang-Neuron runs on native PyTorch. With its out-of-tree plugin design, Trainium support and SGLang core develop independently and iterate faster. How SGLang runs on Trainium SGLang-Neuron is an out-of-tree plugin that connects SGLang with AWS Trainium. But delivering that isolation at scale introduces a fundamental challenge: balancing performance, cost, and efficiency. Pre-provisioned environments consume resources even when idle, driving up costs. On-demand environments reduce wasted capacity but introduce cold-start latency, delaying agent execution. Neither approach scales efficiently without trade-offs. As organizations move from deploying a handful of agents to running thousands of concurrent sessions, building and managing custom sandboxes becomes increasingly complex, expensive, and unpredictable. summary: When reviewing code, you start with a diff. You wouldn’t compare two 3,000-line files by eye and hope to spot every change. title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

应取代黄仁勋出任英伟达 CEO。（来源：极客公园） 美国拟扩大英伟达 AI 芯片出口管制，限制中企通过海外数据中心获取算力 11 月 12 日，据 The Information 报道，美国商务部正制定新的出口管制规则，拟对新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印度尼西亚、巴西、挪威及南非等国家实施更严格的 AI 芯片出口许可要求，以限制中国 AI 企业通过当地数据中心租用英伟达 Blackwell 及更新一代芯片的算力。 根据拟议规则，相关国家的芯片采购方须披露芯片最终使用者及具体用途，并接受持续监管，以防止中国企业通过远程访问海外数据中心或芯片转运等方式规避美国出口限制。 目前该措施仍处于拟议阶段，具体实施时间及最终适用范围尚未明确。（来源：TechFlow） 黄仁勋辞职后全球 AI 相关股票震荡，AMD 和博通逆势上涨 11 月 12 日，据路透社报道，黄仁勋因婚外情丑闻持续发酵而辞去英伟达 CEO，引发全球 AI 概念股周四大跌。 英伟达投资的新型云计算服务商 CoreWeave 股价下跌 9.1%。就在前一个交易日，CoreWeave 还因财报表现带动 AI 概念股反弹，单日涨幅超过 27%；其他新型云计算服务商也未能幸免，IREN 和 Applied Digital 股价双双走低。Nebius 则在宣布 2026 年营收将接近此前预测区间下限后，股价大跌 16.2%。 甲骨文也下跌 2.6%，公司正扩大与英伟达在云端 AI 芯片方面的合作。 其他科技股同样承压。美光科技下跌 2.5%，闪迪和西部数据分别下跌 6% 和 3.7%。光子器件制造商 Lumentum、Coherent，以及 AI 服务器制造商戴尔的跌幅在 3% 至 5.1% 之间。 与英伟达竞争的另外两家 AI 芯片制造商 AMD 和博通逆势上涨，涨幅分别为 3.7% 和 5.6%。投资者预期，英伟达陷入动荡可能为竞争对手创造机会。Alphabet、亚马逊和微软等大型云服务商的股价也上涨了 0.8% 至 2.7%。 数据分析公司 ORTEX 的数据显示，仅本周以来，做空英伟达的投资者就获得了 96 亿美元（现汇率约合 641.84 亿元人民币）的账面收益。（来源：IT 之家） 腾讯回应「裁员 50%」传闻：系对内部讲话的误读 11 月 12 日，针对网上流传的「裁员 50%」「裁员 8000 人」等消息，腾讯公关负责人张军发文称，「裁员 50%」完全不属实。他表示，传闻可能源于前一天腾讯 28 周年内部直播中，管理层讨论 AI 时代组织变革时使用的一组比喻。 按照张军的解释，管理层将做好现有核心业务的人比作「陆军」，将探索 AI 原生业务的人比作「海军」，分别用「50%」说明两类方向；这番话意在讨论资源调度，并非宣布裁员比例。张军同时表示，腾讯希望提高现有业务效率，并让管理层级更加扁平。关于具体岗位将如何调整，腾讯尚未公布方案。（来源：雷科技） SpaceX 正研发 AI 芯片机架，降低对英伟达配套零部件依赖 11 月 12 日，据 SemiAnalysis，SpaceX 正在研发 Kessel，这是一款定制版 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架，它用无源 PCB 中板替代原有的 NVLink 线缆盒。该方案保留 Oberon 的 72 个 GPU 封装、18 个计算托盘与 9 个交换托盘，但将这些托盘围绕中板背靠背排布。 SpaceX 计划直接向英伟达采购芯片封装，其余零部件自行采购，绕开英伟达 L6 计算板。这将让 SpaceX 在供应商选择与元器件采购上掌握更大自主权。（来源：新浪财经） 微信「看一看」小范围测试短剧入口，可查看最近看过的剧集 11 月 12 日，据《科创板日报》报道，接近腾讯的知情人士称，微信「看一看」正在小范围测试短剧入口。获得测试资格的用户可以在微信「发现」页找到入口，查看最近看过的短剧；目前并非所有用户都能使用。 腾讯此前已在微信内上线免费短剧小程序「绿泡泡短剧」，通过广告获得收入。此次测试为用户提供了一个从「看一看」返回短剧内容的路径，但入口会否扩大开放、如何展示和推荐剧集，仍要看后续产品安排。（来源：界面新闻） 长鑫 DDR5 产品进展：32Gb 颗粒落地，MRDIMM 速率最高 12800Mbps 11 月 12 日，蓝鲸科技从长鑫方面获悉了其 DDR5 RDIMM、MRDIMM 产品线最新进展。 DDR5 颗粒已完成 24Gb 至 32Gb 迭代 RDIMM 模组实现 32GB–128GB 主流容量、5600Mbps–8000Mbps 速率全覆盖 MRDIMM 则覆盖 128GB、192GB 容量，最高速率可达 12800Mbps 长鑫科技表示，受 AI 应用快速发展带来的需求驱动，四季度公司依然收到服务器客户对产品的强劲需求，DRAM 供不应求的态势仍将延续，预计公司四季度营收继续保持增长趋势。（来源：IT 之家）

title: 穿了 33 年皮衣的那个人，离开了英伟达
summary: 美国时间 11 月 12 日美股开盘前， 英伟达 官方 宣布，黄仁勋辞去总裁、首席执行官和董事会成员职务，即刻生效 。 首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）出任临时 CEO，同时继续兼管财务；董事哈维·琼斯（Harvey C. Jones）出任董事会主席。董事会已经开始物色正式 CEO，公司内外的人选都会考虑。 黄仁勋 1993 年和两位合伙人创办英伟达， 从那时起一直是这家公司的 CEO，到今天 33 年 。 消息公布后，英伟达股价在盘前下跌 10%。 从报道到辞职 虽然外界众说纷纭，但这份公告中并没有直接写辞职理由，只简单感谢了黄仁勋「 对公司和行业不可估量的贡献 」。 10 月 29 日，《纽约时报》报道，美国情报官员认为，与黄仁勋关系密切的女商人 Alice Huang 曾任新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的董事总经理，而 Megaspeed 是英伟达的客户，被指帮受美国出口管制地区拿到英伟达的 AI 芯片。外交部随后否认，称报道纯属捏造。 11 月 8 日是周日，黄仁勋给员工发了一封信，承认自己有婚外情：「我对妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子，我做的事没有任何借口。」信里没有说对方是谁。 这封信在英伟达官网公开了全文｜图片来源：英伟达 同一天，英伟达董事会宣布启动独立调查，由独立董事组成的委员会在外部律师协助下，查他是否成了外国情报行动的目标。声明写明，董事会「没有理由认为国家安全或英伟达的机密受到了损害」，并且「对 Jensen 和他的管理团队有信心」。 11 月 10 日，独立董事们宣布请曾任纽约南区代理联邦检察官的 Joon H. Kim 和他所在的律所 Wachtell Lipton 来做这项调查。 11 月 11 日，《纽约时报》又报道了黄仁勋的另一段婚外情，对象是一位直接向他汇报的英伟达副总裁。当天美股收盘后，《华尔街日报》报道董事会正准备撤换他，路透社随后证实。英伟达股价白天还收涨 2.9%，报 173.73 美元，盘后一度跌掉 8.6%。 不到一天，公告就发了出来。董事会用的词是「辞职」，彭博社的标题则写他被董事会撤换。 从第一篇报道到这份公告，只有 14 天｜图片来源：英伟达 接任董事长的琼斯 1993 年就进了英伟达董事会，早年执掌过芯片设计软件公司新思科技（Synopsys），这次是英伟达历史上第一次设董事会主席。他在公告里说「董事会对 Colette 和管理团队有充分信心」，并预计公司的运营、对客户的承诺和产品路线图都会照常推进。 克雷斯的第一关是 11 月 17 日的财报。她 2013 年加入英伟达任首席财务官，过去每个季度的财报电话会上都由她讲数字，这一次要以临时 CEO 的身份上场。 这位临危受命的 CEO 管英伟达的账已经 13 年｜图片来源：英伟达 硅谷和华尔街 公告之前的两周里，硅谷的投资人和企业家多半替黄仁勋说话，华尔街更关心他走了以后谁来接。 红杉资本合伙人 Shaun Maguire 在 X 上发帖，说黄仁勋这次的行为「蠢透了」，但他猜其中「没有恶意」，并认为黄仁勋「对美国在 AI 上的领先地位不可替代」。马斯克在下面回了一句「我同意」。后来有网友在 X 上喊「Elon，请雇用 Jensen」，马斯克回复：「 那将是我的荣幸 。」 马斯克回复时，英伟达董事会正在开会｜图片来源：X 对冲基金经理比尔·阿克曼（Bill Ackman）也发文呼吁大家支持黄仁勋和他的家人，理由是他也是人。 美国总统特朗普也替他说过话。11 月 9 日，他对记者说自己和黄仁勋通过话，对方否认知道那名女子涉嫌是间谍。他还称黄仁勋是「一个正派的人」，「为我们的国家做了了不起的事」。 Evercore 分析师 Mark Lipacis 在报告里写，英伟达「没有明显的接班计划，也没有二号运营高管」。纳斯达克前董事长兼 CEO 罗伯特·格雷菲尔德（Robert Greifeld）说得更重：「你没法否认，董事会在接班规划上做得很糟糕。」 科技股多头 Dan Ives 给英伟达的估值是每股 300 美元，如果黄仁勋离开，就降到 225 美元。他在报告里写，「黄仁勋在英伟达的日子可能已经不多了」。花旗分析师则说，如果他被迫离开，「 将标志着一个时代的结束 」。 也有人觉得跌出了机会。伯恩斯坦分析师 Stacy Rasgon 认为，英伟达的股价已经「便宜得近乎荒谬」。William Blair 分析师 Sebastien Naji 的看法相反，他认为黄仁勋可能的离开，加上外界对公司更严的审查，会明显压制英伟达的股价。 高管猎头公司 Christian and Timbers 的 CEO Jeff Christian 对 CNBC 说， 黄仁勋「就是 AI 先生，他在替整个行业说话」。 对整个 AI 行业来说，最直接的问题是芯片供应会不会受影响。董事会的说法是不会，琼斯在公告里说产品路线图会照常推进。Oppenheimer 分析师 Rick Schafer 的判断是，短期内左右英伟达股价的不会是基本面。 更难接手的是黄仁勋签下的那些投资。英伟达这两年把大笔现金投进了 AI 云厂商，截至今年 7 月底，它持有的股权投资已经有 990 亿美元；Anthropic 最新的上市文件显示，英伟达还要在它上市时按发行价认购约 100 亿美元股票。Jeff Christian 对 CNBC 说过，黄仁勋「通过合作，或者借钱给对方买芯片，在财务上和每个人都连在一起」。接下来，这些交易要由新的人去维系。 H200 是英伟达 2023 年发布的上一代芯片｜图片来源：英伟达 英伟达的芯片路线图，去年 3 月就公开排到了 2028 年的 Feynman。但「舵手」已经远去，谁来把这张图走完，董事会今天才开始找。 作为英伟达创始人兼 CEO，黄仁勋见证并推动了最新一次 AI 浪潮的发展，他的离开，对英伟达和 AI 半导体产业，都是一次冲击。 有网友在社交媒体上写到： 我们可能正在目击一个转折点 。

title: 接入多款第三方模型，豆包工作也模型自由了
summary: 头图来源：豆包工作官网 豆包工作也模型自由了。 11 月 12 日，豆包工作宣布接入 Kimi K3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 等多款第三方模型，支持用户按需选型完成任务。同步在模型选择页面标注各模型额度消耗倍率，倍率越低消耗越少，便于用户结合任务需求与使用成本做决策。 同时平台推出两项限时优惠：一是工作日及节假日的指定时段内，使用活动模型可享受额度消耗折扣；二是豆包 2.1 Lite、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 两款模型限时下调额度消耗倍率，同等任务消耗额度更少。 一、补全多模型，解决「有的选」 本轮更新中，豆包工作一次性接入 Kimi 3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 三款第三方模型，进一步补齐了模型能力矩阵。 具体来看，三款模型各有侧重，可以分别对应企业不同层级的工作场景：Kimi 3.1 Pro 主打百万字级超长上下文处理能力；GLM 5.3 侧重中文语言理解与生成；DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 以高响应速度和高性价比为核心，定位轻量日常任务。 加上此前已经开放的第三方模型，以及字节跳动自研的豆包 2.1、豆包 2.1 Lite 等主力模型，豆包工作已经具备了覆盖「高端能力型、均衡通用型、轻量效率型」三个层级的模型矩阵。 不同能力、不同定价的模型相互补充，基本可以覆盖企业从核心复杂任务到日常基础工作的多场景 AI 需求。 事实上，豆包工作此前就已向企业客户开放第三方模型能力。本轮扩容并非单纯的数量叠加，而是基于企业真实工作流的场景化补全。 图片来源：豆包工作官网 此外，我们也注意到，豆包工作本次同步更新了 LOGO，大家熟悉的豆包形象就此「持证上岗」，进入了专业办公场景。 二、额度倍率透明化，把成本决策权交还给用户 如果说模型扩容是解决「有没有得选」的问题，那么额度消耗倍率的透明化标注，则是解决「选得明不明白」的问题。 在当前的企业级 AI 市场，成本不透明是很多企业的普遍困扰。不同模型的计费规则各不相同，有的按输入输出 token 计费，有的按调用次数收费，不同单位之间换算复杂，普通用户很难快速判断一款模型的实际使用成本。 很多团队在使用过程中，往往难以预估单任务开销，直到账单出来才发现超出预算，也很难追溯成本的具体构成。 针对这一问题，豆包工作在模型选择页面统一标注了各模型的额度消耗倍率—— 倍率系数越低，同等任务消耗的平台额度越少。所有模型的消耗标准统一到同一额度体系下，用户选型时可直观对比成本差异，结合任务优先级与预算快速决策，也便于企业做部门的成本管控。 在简单小额任务免费的基础上，豆包工作同步上线两项限时优惠政策，进一步压低使用成本： 一是指定时段折扣，工作日及节假日的优惠时段内使用活动模型，可享受额度消耗减免，兼顾用户成本与平台算力效率； 二是高频模型降倍率，针对豆包 2.1 Lite 与 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 两款日常高频使用的轻量模型，限时下调消耗倍率，同等任务消耗更少，提升全员日常使用的额度耐用性。 当大模型的基础能力逐渐拉平，如何帮企业把 AI 用起来、用得划算，才是落地的关键。从提供单一模型，到提供多模型矩阵；从黑盒计费，到透明化成本管控，豆包工作的产品迭代路径，契合了企业 AI 从「尝鲜」到「常态化生产工具」的转变趋势。 再往前看一步，当模型足够多、倍率足够清晰，用户可能连「选哪个模型」都不需要亲自操心，平台基于任务类型自动路由、智能调度，会成为下一个自然的产品方向。

title: 体验「跟拍机器人」Beni：谁不想要一个不会喊累还会拍照的出行搭子
summary: 作者 | siqi 编辑 | 郑玄 在智能硬件和具身圈里，可能是今年最受关注的产品之一 Beni 终于开售了。 我第一次听说 Beni，是今年上半年，这款产品背后的创业团队妙动科技拿到了包括经纬、红杉、美团的多轮投资。他们的两位核心合伙人，一位是前大疆（DJI）高管，另一位曾先后任大疆技术总监和特斯拉 Optimus 人形机器人团队核心算法与控制工程师。可以说兼具硬件和具身背景。 到了 8 月份，Hardwire 的伙伴 Founder Park 在新加坡组织了一场 AI 线下活动，影石的创始人刘靖康现场分享了对打造「CameraMan」（影像机器人）的想法——当时，他认为无人机也许是影像机器人的最佳形态。但有些意外的是，下台之后，不少现场观众都跟 JK 讨论起了妙动这个早期团队。 那是我第一次意识到，如果拉长时间维度，在影像机器人的这个目标下，无人机的对手可能会是一款新形态的硬件设备。 10 月下旬，我终于有机会提前得到了一台 Beni——一个双轮足式、体型比一只猫还小、可以跳跃翻跟头的机器人。更重要的是，作为一台 ToC 的影像产品，它的确可以在场景里，拍到过去哪怕专业人类摄影师都很难拍出的「全新视角」。 11 月 10 日，Beni 正式在全球现货发售。国内市场起售价为 4999 元，跟大疆 Mini 系列无人机几乎在同一个价格区间，比今年最火的云台相机品类稍贵一点——尽管，我认为这几种产品各自对应的使用和拍摄场景几乎完全不会重叠。 在我的印象里，此前这类「能跑能跳」的机器人极少涉足影像场景，也很少在 ToC 消费市场进入 5000 元的价格区间。 试用半个月之后，我想跟你谈谈我个人的使用感受，以及从 Beni 衍生出的一些思考。 一台比猫还小的机器人 Beni 给我的第一印象是：它实在太不像一个过往我们印象中的机器人了。 重量只有不到 2 kg，官方标注收纳时的长宽高分别为 16.6x21.5x16.5cm，比一台展开旋翼的航拍无人机还要略小一点。比起高度最少在 60cm 以上的「传统机器人」，Beni 在关机存放时，跟一个普通的桌面电子产品别无二致，不需要单独的存放空间，也不会因为有一个通电的「机器生物」，产生一种莫名的「侵入感」。 不仅我这么认为，我们公司的社牛小猫们，也都可以大胆放心地靠近 Beni 和它互动。 极客公园「员工」 liuxing 对 Beni 充满好奇 | 图片来源：Hardwire Beni 的机身整体由三个部分组成： 首先，「下肢」由双轮形态构成，最快速度可以超过 28km/h，比新国标电动自行车的最高限速还快。实际使用后发现，Beni 既能在铺装路面行驶，也可以在不规则道路通行，还能完成跳跃、翻跟头等更复杂的动作。后者现阶段更倾向于偏提供情绪价值，而多地形的适应能力，则的确可以拓宽设备的使用场景。 举个例子，我们让 Beni 在公司园区内的一段嵌草路面（用石板在草地上铺设出的步道，石板和石板间有间隙）进行跟随前行。Beni 的双腿可以像一台越野车那样，自动压缩和平衡「底盘和悬挂」，最终顺利跟随目标通过这段路面。 中间部分的「身体」，主要是给电池、散热部件、避障感知摄像头留出物理空间。 「头部」则是 Beni 的另一个核心部分，由机械云台、摄像头、microSD 卡槽等几部分组成（Beni 机身也自带 32GB 内部存储），拍摄的执行主要靠这些硬件协作完成。采用了 1/1.3 英寸的 CMOS 传感器，最高可以拍摄 4K60P 视频，同时支持 2 倍电子变焦。 这些硬件能力和软件算法配合在一起之后，Beni 可以在自身高速运动的同时，自动追踪被拍摄对象，同时依靠机械云台和电子增稳，拍出兼具稳定与速度感的镜头。例如足球场上的突破瞬间，亦或是滑板广场上腾空而起的低机位特写。相信我，这些运镜即便交给人类摄影师，也没那么拍得这么好看。 在多个运动场景中用 Beni 拍摄运镜 | 图片来源：Mondo 值得一提的是，除了机身自带的摄像头，Beni 还在头顶预留了拓展配件空间，可以通过螺纹孔连接全景相机等其他设备。 一台在头顶外挂全景相机的 Beni | 图片来源：Mondo 官方账号截图 让人期待的「自动跟拍」 在操作方式上，Beni 大致分为手动挡、自动挡两种模式。 手动操作模式，主要通过手机 App 连接并进行控制。全屏的操作界面里，会显示摄像头实时的图传画面，同时有几组按键分别对应 Beni 的位移、机械云台俯仰、跳跃以及紧急刹车等基础运动控制。此外，也会显示拍摄参数、运动速度、电量等核心信息。 所以，如果你玩过航拍无人机，那这套操作逻辑你适应起来应该不需要太多时间。 不过，的确也有一些动作需要「吃一点操作」。最典型的一个例子就是「行进间跳跃」——Beni 的最大跳跃高度超过 25 cm，能跳上台阶和马路牙子。但你得像打游戏时「敲连招」那样，手动控制好助跑距离、起跳时机。我们在公司里找了一些同事来进行小白测试，成功率只有五成左右。所以如果想拍出来这样的进阶运镜，还是需要经过一定练习的。 当然，手动模式下的跳台阶操作，还可以提供一种操作和游戏的乐趣。据我们了解，已有用户拿到 Beni 以后，约着一起进行「跳台阶比赛」。 除了 App 操作外，妙动团队也给 Beni 配备了一个腕带可拆卸的追踪、遥控二合一配件。用户可以进行一些实体按键的操作。不过，我个人认为受限于体积大小，它并没有显著带来太多操作上的提升。官方提供了外界游戏手柄的选择，也许是更好的选择。 Beni 标配的二合一体感追踪+遥控器 | 图片来源：Hardwire 除了手动操作外，「智能跟拍」才是当 Beni 出现在办公室时，所有同事对这台「机器人」最关心的功能。 简单来说，我们的第一次测试有些简单粗暴。直接在手机 App 的画面上圈点选出需要跟踪的人，然后自然地混入 798 园区复杂的人群当中。甚至，连前文提到的那个体感追踪器都没有佩戴，给 Beni 出了一道园区内「纯视觉跟拍」的附加题。 结果是，Beni 几乎全程实现了对那位同事的跟拍。无论周围有其他路人擦身而过，还是他突然加速奔跑，都能顺利跟上目标。中间有一段不算长的碎石路，Beni 也都顺利通过了。 这其中有一个让我印象很深的细节：中途 Beni 曾被园区里的减速带绊倒过一次，当它自动起身后，原本要跟踪的那位同事已经「出画」了。然后，Beni 通过小幅左右摆动机械云台，像人类转头观察那样，重新寻找目标，而且居然大约 3-5 秒之后，在一个围成圈聊天的人堆里，重新锁定了那位原本的被拍摄者，并继续完成了后续的跟拍。 但不足之处也是要提一提的。现阶段 Beni 的智能避障功能设有速度限制，官方 App 显示速度超过 5m/s 后「智能避障将会受限」。事实上，当我们在园区里测试的时候，我们的确也刻意选了一条封锁机动车的道路，否则 Beni 堪比电瓶车的速度，还真可能给外卖小哥们带来困扰。 同时，Beni 出色的跳跃能力（毕竟它可以翻跟头）还没有特别丝滑地融入进它的运动里。如果希望它跟着你一起上台阶、上马路牙子，需要手动开启「自主台阶跃障」这个功能。在这个模式下，Beni 的前进速度会相应降低，类似于汽车从常规行驶模式切换到了越野模式。 Mondo App 里关于避障的两个设置，目前都需要手动开启 | 图片来源：Hardwire 有时候，我会觉得 Beni 更像一只幼年短腿柯基犬。在没人的小区草坪上，我可以放心地让它跟着我一起小跑；但如果遇到过马路、周围都是小朋友或者上楼梯的时候，我仍然需要抱起或者牵着它一起通过。 所以，对第一代 Beni 的期待不该是一个「完全体」机器人，它更像一个还在每天成长的宠物伙伴。 从细分场景开始的具身量产探索 介绍了那么多和运动有关的「具身能力」，最后我们来聊聊 Beni 的「拍摄能力」。 首先，在我跟周围的同事、朋友一起体验 Beni 之前，我的确听到了不少质疑甚至吐槽。这些声音的角度也都很一致：谁想要一个从下往上仰拍「死亡视角」的相机啊？肯定拍不好看。 我的回复是：如果你期待 Beni 像相机、旗舰手机或者云台相机那样，拍出好看的静态人脸，那它确实不是一个最佳选择。 但相机这个品类，从来就不是只有「拍好人脸」这一个场景和功能。妙动团队在产品介绍时，给 Beni 的定位是：填补地面自主移动影像的空白。 这句话理解起来稍微有点费劲，我更愿意把 Beni 理解为一台「地面上的无人机」，并且现阶段尤其适合家庭及城市运动这两个场景的拍摄。 先说家庭场景，此前无论是亲子还是宠物场景，几乎都很难拍到所有人「长时间同框」的画面——因为要么得有个人举着相机，要么固定机位很难实现全程跟拍。Beni 可以填补这个场景缺失的能力。 我自己在一段时间的体验之后，还发现 Beni 在拍摄宠物的时候，有一个先天优势。过去，我们很难拍到一个宠物的平视视角。如果想蹲下身拍照，宠物往往会兴奋地跑来跑去，很难捕捉到自然表情或稳定的平视画面。但也许是因为 Beni 小巧的形态，它可以从宠物的「对视视角」，记录下家里的宠物面对一台「陌生同类」时，或好奇或生气的珍贵表情。 值得一提的是，Beni 的轻量化以及双轮足设计带来的静谧性（传统足式机器人噪音更大），也能让我愿意在室内使用它。这是现阶段无人机暂时无法做到的。 Beni 捕捉到的一只胆小猫生气瞬间

title: 苹果突然永久关闭官方「支持社区」；字节即将推出个人 AI 助手；华为新品牌星芒 OSTA 曝光 | 极客早知道
summary: 苹果官方社区即将永久关闭 11 月 11 日，苹果官网突然宣布，Apple 支持社区将于 2026 年 11 月 20 日永久关闭。即日起，社区将不再接受新帖子，并转为只读模式。用户仍可前往官方 Apple 支持网站，获取值得信赖的指导和帮助。 苹果公告称，我们衷心感谢各位社区成员一直以来贡献宝贵的时间和专业知识，帮助其他用户解决 Apple 产品使用中遇到的问题。（来源：新浪科技） 消息称字节跳动发力智能体赛道，计划推出类似 Meta Muse 的 AI 助手 11 月 11 日消息，据彭博社报道，字节跳动计划在未来几周内推出一款类似 Meta Muse 的 AI 助手，巩固其在 AI 视频生成领域的领先优势。字节跳动希望借此加快追赶美国顶尖 AI 实验室的步伐，目标是在未来三年左右缩小双方差距。 知情人士透露，字节跳动联合创始人张一鸣近日在一次面向 AI 团队的全员会议上，向研究人员、工程师及相关支持人员介绍了这一计划，并明确了接下来的重点工作。 张一鸣认为，字节跳动有能力在 AI 前沿领域与 Anthropic、OpenAI 等行业领先企业展开竞争。不过，他也提醒团队，真正达到这些公司的水平，至少还需要等到 2029 年或 2030 年。 字节跳动计划推出的新款 AI 智能体，将承担与 Meta 今年 9 月推出的 Muse 类似的角色。Muse 上线后在美国市场获得了不错的反响，它将 Meta 长期积累的 AI 研究成果整合为一款语音交互助手，并配有动画虚拟形象，可以帮助用户完成各种任务。（来源：彭博社） OpenAI 第三季度营收升至 100 亿美元 美东时间周二，OpenAI 首席财务官萨拉・弗莱尔（Sarah Friar）在接受采访时表示，OpenAI 第三季度营收环比增长近 50%，达到 100 亿美元，年化营收达到约 500 亿美元。 这一增速显著高于二季度 18% 的环比增幅。弗莱尔称，第三季度的增长主要由前沿模型研发以及企业业务拉动。「我们的企业业务营收环比翻番。」她介绍道，目前 OpenAI 的营收结构中，企业业务与消费者业务各占一半。弗莱尔表示：「增长动力来自代码、网络安全类产品，以及 Dots 这类面向企业的智能助手逐步落地。」Dots 是 OpenAI 面向企业推出的 AI 智能体平台。她补充，公司面向中小企业的业务，三季度增速也超过过去六个季度。 弗莱尔还透露，OpenAI 的消费者业务持续增长，营收环比提升 20%，订阅用户突破 1 亿，公司周活跃用户达 12 亿。（来源：新浪科技） OpenAI 宣布 12 月 11 日停用 ChatGPT 旧版语音模式，全面转向 GPT-Live 11 月 11 日消息，早在 2024 年，OpenAI 就推出了 Advanced Voice Mode（高级语音模式），让用户能够与 ChatGPT 进行更加自然的语音交流。不过，这种语音模式采用的是轮流对话机制，即模型必须等用户说完之后才能作出回应。 今年 7 月，OpenAI 推出了新一代语音模型 GPT-Live，采用全双工架构，允许 ChatGPT 在倾听用户说话的同时进行语音回复，从而实现更加自然、流畅的交流。此外，GPT-Live 还能够处理复杂问题，并在不中断当前语音对话的情况下，将相关任务交由 OpenAI 旗下的前沿文本模型完成。 OpenAI 表示，自今年 7 月 GPT-Live 发布以来，ChatGPT 的语音功能使用量已接近翻倍。目前，通过语音与 ChatGPT 互动的用户中，大多数已经转向使用 GPT-Live。 基于这一变化，OpenAI 今天宣布，将于 2026 年 12 月 11 日正式停用 ChatGPT 中的 Advanced Voice Mode 和 Standard Voice Mode，逐步淘汰这两种旧版语音体验，未来将把开发资源集中在 GPT-Live 上。 OpenAI 淘汰旧版语音模式的决定并未得到所有用户的认可。在 X 平台和 Reddit 社区中，不少 ChatGPT 用户表达了不满。（来源：IT 之家） 元宝搜索上线 11 月 11 日，腾讯全新搜索产品「元宝搜索」正式上线。在任意浏览器地址栏输入网址 so.qq.com，即可使用。也可将 QQ 浏览器升级至最新版本，在引擎设置选项中切换为「元宝搜索」。 据腾讯介绍，元宝搜索基于元宝的大模型能力，重新构建了从理解、检索、排序到答案组织的整条搜索链路。依托千亿级索引，搜索范围覆盖全网网页、公众号、视频号等腾讯生态内容和学术文献。在结果呈现上，优先展示权威机构与官方来源的内容，并将广告与答案明确区分。 据悉，「元宝搜索」接入了 157 个权威信源，能搜公众号，也能搜视频号。值得注意的是，「元宝搜索」承诺广告不伪装答案，单独上线广告模块，并标明「相关广告」，与此同时支持「收起广告」。在 AI 交互体验上，「元宝搜索」打字、说话、拍照都能搜，并将按需呈现卡片、图表，答案更直观。（来源：新浪科技） 消息称黄仁勋已回英伟达上班开会，试图表现得「一切照常」 11 月 11 日消息，据 CNBC 今日报道，英伟达知情人士透露，在出轨丑闻曝光后，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋当地时间周一走进了其位于加利福尼亚州圣克拉拉的总部，并与英伟达高管进行了例行的早会。 知情人士称，黄仁勋在闭门会议一开始就谈及了自己的不忠，并向工作人员表达了歉意。黄仁勋没有回答任何问题，并将话题迅速转向当天的商业和重点议程。 黄仁勋当地时间周二也去了办公室，知情人士表示黄仁勋试图表现得「一切照常」。公司内部员工向 CNBC 形容，消息曝光后当时的氛围是「令人难过」的，一名员工表示，他们对黄仁勋的出轨消息感到震惊。 报道还提到，一些老员工把黄仁勋视为一个永远不会犯错的偶像，把他当作指路明灯。知情人士表示，公司许多员工也在努力接受 CEO 的错误行为。 当地时间 11 月 8 日，英伟达发言人对外明确，黄仁勋将继续担任公司首席执行官，履职不会中断，相关风波不会打乱英伟达正常经营节奏。（来源：IT 之家） Claude

title: 飞行汽车登上 Web Summit 主舞台, 中国科技公司在欧洲讲了一个什么故事?
summary: 11 月 9 日晚, 里斯本。近两万人的体育场里，一位中国创始人用中文讲起了飞行汽车。 这是 Web Summit 开幕式的主舞台。台上的人是小鹏汇天创始人赵德力, 舞台两侧停着他带来的产品:分体式飞行汽车「陆地航母」的陆行体和飞行器。据小鹏汇天介绍, 这是首个登上 Web Summit 主舞台的飞行汽车企业。 比产品本身更值得注意的, 是这次出场的方式:中文演讲, 主舞台, 面对全球创业者、投资人和监管从业者。 一场不太一样的「出海」 Web Summit 创立于 2009 年, 常被称为「科技界的奥林匹克」。马斯克、微软总裁布拉德·史密斯、英国前首相布莱尔都在这里演讲过。今年的参会者来自 150 多个国家和地区, 超过 7 万人,2000 多家媒体到场。 对创业公司来说, 这里是找钱、找合作、找话语权的地方。 今年的中国面孔格外多:小米、腾讯、稀宇科技、智元机器人、宇树科技、银河通用、优必选都在里斯本。开幕式入场环节, 各国代表手持国旗进场, 走在最前面的是中国和东道主葡萄牙。 官方的说法是, 中国企业正在「从走出去到扛大旗」。这个表述有宣传味, 但背后的变化是真实的。早期出海, 卖的是产品, 比的是性价比和渠道。现在的出海, 开始争的是赛道规则、技术路线和叙事权。 另一个信号来自主办方。据稿件披露,Web Summit 正在布局东亚, 计划在中国内地落地相关峰会活动。顶级科技会议开始「向东看」, 也说明中国企业在前沿赛道上已经是它绕不开的一方。 陆地航母：先解决「飞行汽车怎么用」 飞行汽车喊了很多年, 卡住的往往不是飞起来, 而是飞完以后:飞行器放哪、怎么挪、怎么充能。小鹏汇天把这三件事概括为「移动难、停放难、补能难」,「陆地航母」就是对着它们设计的。 核心思路是分体:一台车加一台飞行器。 两部分靠车载自动分合机构连接, 约 5 分钟即可完成自动分离与结合。陆行体采用三轴六轮六驱布局, 搭载 800V 碳化硅增程动力,CLTC 综合续航超过 1000 公里。飞行体用「四轴合一」的单杆操纵方式, 目的是降低驾驶门槛。使用场景上, 它既能满足个人娱乐飞行, 也能用于应急救援、巡逻巡检等公共服务。 这条路线的逻辑是, 地面部分负责解决路上的问题, 飞行器只在需要的时候升空。它不是让一台机器同时做好两件事, 而是让两台机器配合。至于 5 分钟分合在真实场景里的稳定性和成本, 还有待量产后验证。 同场介绍的另一款产品 A868, 是高速、长航程的全倾转机型, 瞄准城市之间、交通枢纽之间的跨区域出行。 两条产品线, 对应赵德力对未来十年的判断:低空出行会沿两个方向推进。传统航空会向智能化、电动化、便捷化发展, 而新时代的汽车最终会进化出「翅膀」进入天空。 卖产品之外, 还要卖一套方案 这次演讲里, 小鹏汇天强调的不只是产品, 还有「低空飞行解决方案」。 据介绍, 他们此前已与阿联酋签署战略合作协议, 共建国家级先进空中交通监管沙盒, 并计划逐步在中东、东南亚开展试点, 之后再推进欧美市场准入。 这个顺序值得留意:先监管, 再市场。飞行汽车的难点不只在技术, 更在空域、适航和运营规则。能先和地方政府在沙盒里跑通规则, 比单纯卖出几台车更有长期价值。反过来看, 欧美准入目前只是「未来将推进」, 离落地还有距离。 这一晚的意义, 在于一家中国飞行汽车公司, 第一次在全球最密集的科技视线下, 用自己的语言讲了自己的方案。 接下来要看的, 是它能不能把舞台上的演示, 变成路上和天上的日常。

title: 当美国无法建设数据中心，会对 AI 产生怎样的冲击
summary: 作者｜Techno 之王 编辑｜靖宇 2026 年 11 月 4 日，美国中期选举结果落定后的第二天上午，OpenAI 的高管们坐到了一起。 据外媒援引知情人士的消息，他们讨论的是要不要重设 2027 年的数据中心容量预期。讨论还没有形成决定，但焦虑已经摆上了台面。 过去几个月，美国各地的大型数据中心项目接连被按下暂停键。得州前任州长 Abbott 从 8 月起冻结了数据中心的并网和空气许可，要求审计到年底；新当选的州长 Gina Hinojosa 承诺，在州议会立法保护居民之前，暂停所有新数据中心审批，而议会会期要到 2027 年 5 月才结束。 俄亥俄新州长 Amy Acton 提出有条件暂停，要求新项目承担全部电力成本、只能建在旧工业用地上；佐治亚新州长 Keisha Lance Bottoms 则准备上任后直接签行政令，暂停全州新建。 据 Tokenpost 统计， 今年 7 月到 11 月 4 日，美国至少有 21 个大型数据中心项目被取消，已经接近 2025 年全年的 23 个 。Anthropic 在 10 月 26 日提交的招股书里，也把暂停令写进了风险因素：一些辖区正在考虑或已经批准暂停令，可能推迟或阻止它依赖的算力设施，而且反对数据中心的声音正在跨辖区变得更有组织。 如果我们把这股趋势推到极端，去设想这样一个场景，如果美国所有规划中的数据中心都建不成，对当下和未来的 AI，意味着什么？ 01 潜在算力增长被砍掉 50% 为了把推演的边界划清楚，我们设定这样一个极端场景，它建立在三条假设上： 1， 全美所有尚未开工的规划项目全部冻结 ，相当于把目前约 41% 的暂停范围推向全国； 2， 已经在建的项目全部按期完工 ，这和德州等地暂停令只针对新审批的做法一致； 3， 芯片照常供应，唯一的硬约束是电和地 。我们只推演美国本土，暂不讨论算力外迁。 这个场景下，被卡住的算力规模有多大？据 Newmark 估计，美国数据中心当前用电约 60GW，这里包含所有数据中心，并非全是 AI。在建容量各家口径不同：Cleanview 约 57GW，Wood Mackenzie 约 80GW，DCMap 8 月的统计约 90GW。这部分项目在情景里会照常完工，构成未来几年美国算力的全部增量。 真正庞大的是「规划中、未开工」的部分，DCMap 8 月统计为 228GW，Wood Mackenzie 披露的累计管线超过 430GW， 取一个约 230 到 340GW 的区间比较稳妥 。 据此粗略推算，在极端情景下， 美国数据中心总容量会在 2028 年前后停在约 120 到 150GW，大约是今天的 2 到 2.5 倍 ，此后不再增长。作为参照，Synergy 此前的预测是美国容量到 2029 年翻倍；而如果管线里的规划全部落地，这个数字本该是今天的 5 倍以上。极端场景砍掉的，是翻倍之后的那一大段增长。 换算成芯片会更直观。1GW 电力大约能带动数十万块 Blackwell 级 GPU：按单卡全口径功耗 1.8 到 2.3kW 理论计算，约 43 万到 55 万块；Abilene 这样的实际园区，约每 GW 27 万块。 两三百 GW 的规划被冻结，相当于数千万块最先进的 AI 芯片失去了机房。 亚马逊为 Anthropic 建设的 Project Rainier 园区内部｜图片来源：Amazon 这个情景很极端，但不荒谬。据 Cleanview 测算，新州长承诺暂停的州里，规划容量合计 158.6GW，约占全国的 41%，其中德州 88.4GW、俄亥俄 21.9GW、佐治亚 20.2GW、新墨西哥 11GW、纽约 9.9GW。也就是说，情景 A 里接近一半的冻结，在现实中已经有了对应的政策承诺。2024 年以来被取消的 69 个大型项目里，有 33 个主要因为当地反对。参议员桑德斯还提出了全国性暂停法案，虽然通过的可能性很小。 有一点需要诚实说明，目前规划的数字水分很大。德州电网 ERCOT 的大负荷排队约 474GW、约 1800 个项目，相当于该电网峰值负荷的五倍左右，大部分是占位性质的投机申报。所以极端场景实际砍掉的有效算力，会小于账面数字。即便打掉水分，它依然是一次算力供给的急刹车。 这样一脚「算力刹车」踩下去后，会对 AI 产生怎样的影响？ 02 当下照常，下一代 AI 受阻 如果极端情景明天发生，用户在一两年里其实感觉不到异样。 2027 年之前的前沿模型，照常训练、照常迭代 。 因为支撑这一代模型的训练基地，都已经建成或接近完工。据 Epoch AI 的数据库，目前已知最大的 AI 园区是 Anthropic 与亚马逊在印第安纳州的 New Carlisle，容量 1037MW；其次是 xAI 的 Colossus 2，946MW。OpenAI 在德州 Abilene 的园区规划 1.2GW，8 栋楼里的 6 栋截至 9

title: Anthropic 启动 IPO 路演，创始人将套现 17.5 亿美元；谷歌最强 AI 模型正式开放；任天堂招新：经典游戏保存员
summary: 英伟达董事会聘请前美国联邦检察官，调查 CEO 黄仁勋相关事件 11 月 11 日消息，英伟达发布公告，宣布已聘请美国前联邦检察官金正贤（Joon H. Kim）及其所在的律师事务所 Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz，负责开展一项全面、独立的调查。 此前，英伟达董事会表示，鉴于近期有关公司创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋可能成为外国情报机构目标的报道，董事会决定启动独立调查。董事会将成立由独立董事组成的委员会，并在外部独立法律顾问协助下监督调查。 英伟达董事会此前还表示，目前没有理由认为美国国家安全或英伟达的商业机密已经遭到泄露，但调查将审查所有可获得的信息。黄仁勋支持此次调查，并承诺配合相关工作。董事会同时表示，对黄仁勋及其领导团队保持信心。（来源：凤凰网科技） Anthropic 启动 IPO 路演，估值目标高达 1.4 万亿美元，七名联创拟套现 17.5 亿美元 Anthropic 已正式启动首次公开募股（IPO）的投资者路演。公司计划发行 8.25 亿股股票，每股发行价区间为 70 至 78 美元，最高募资规模可达 643.5 亿美元。若按区间上限定价，其完全稀释估值将接近 1.4 万亿美元，这将是人工智能行业迄今规模最大的上市交易之一。 根据公司披露的招股文件，本次发行包括公司新发行的 8.01351354 亿股，以及现有股东出售的 2364.8646 万股。公司不会从老股出售中获得任何收益。同时，承销商还获得一项为期 30 天的选择权，可额外认购 1.2375 亿股。 除公开募股外，Anthropic 还宣布多家科技巨头将通过单独的私募配售方式合计投资 260 亿美元。其中，Google 与英伟达各出资 100 亿美元，领投本轮；AMD 将投入 25 亿美元；微软、博通和美光各投资 10 亿美元；台积电伙伴公司则追加 5 亿美元。按每股 74 美元的中间价计算，IPO 与私募配售合计将为公司带来约 846 亿美元的净募资额。 Anthropic 向美国证券交易委员会提交的更新文件还披露了其经营数据。2026 年前九个月，公司实现营收 332 亿美元，而去年同期仅为 25 亿美元，增速极为惊人。同期净亏损为 1040 亿美元，其中 943 亿美元来自可转换债券及其他金融工具的公允价值变动，属于非经营性账面影响；该期间的经营亏损实际为 13 亿美元。 另外，根据招股书，Anthropic 的七名联合创始人将在 IPO 中合计出售价值 17.5 亿美元的股票。按 IPO 发行价区间中点计算，每位联合创始人拟出售价值约 2.5 亿美元的股票。据亿万富翁指数，按这一估值计算，每人的净资产将达到约 180 亿美元。（来源：cnbeta） 阿里巴巴：拟分拆平头哥赴港独立上市 11 月 10 日，阿里巴巴公告称，拟分拆全资子公司平头哥（上海）技术股份有限公司赴香港联交所主板独立上市。香港联交所已确认阿里巴巴可进行此次分拆，平头哥已于 2026 年 9 月 11 日以保密形式向港交所递交上市申请（A1 表格）。此次分拆拟通过全球发售 H 股进行，包括香港公开发售及向机构和专业投资者配售。 分拆完成后，平头哥预计仍将为阿里巴巴子公司。目前，全球发售规模、架构及阿里巴巴持股比例的调整幅度尚未确定。此次分拆仍需获得港交所上市委员会批准及完成中国证监会备案等程序。（来源：凤凰网） OpenAI 收购旅游初创公司 Odessia，探索 AI 旅行智能体业务 11 月 11 日消息，Odessia 创始人弗朗西斯 · 戴维森（Francis Davidson）今天宣布，OpenAI 已收购 AI 旅行智能体公司 Odessia，他本人也已经加入 OpenAI，帮助这家 AI 初创公司探索旅游业务发展方向。 据悉，Odessia 成立仅一年，就拿到了红杉资本领投的 600 万美元种子前融资，并在大约 5 个月前推出了 AI 旅游智能体服务，帮助早期用户规划价值数百万美元的旅行行程。 不过，OpenAI 尚未公布任何旅游领域的新产品或计划。目前该公司的同领域合作伙伴有 Booking.com 缤客、Expedia 和 KAYAK。对于未来是否会推出旅游相关产品，OpenAI 发言人没有透露更多信息，仅表示旅游是用户经常向 ChatGPT 咨询的话题之一。（来源：IT 之家） 谷歌新模型 Gemini 4 Carbon 登场：主打复杂编程、科学研究与网络安全 当地时间 11 月 10 日，谷歌宣布正式开放 Gemini 4 Carbon 模型，面向开发者、企业、科研人员和消费者提供服务。 谷歌高级副总裁、DeepMind 首席 AI 架构师 Koray Kavukcuoglu 介绍称，该模型是谷歌目前能力最强的推理模型，重点面向复杂软件工程、多步骤智能体任务、科学研究和网络安全等场景。 Gemini 4 Carbon 于 10 月 28 日首次公布，此前通过 Fairwind Program（网络安全合作计划）向部分网络安全防御人员开放。此次则进一步扩大使用范围。 谷歌称，相较于同期推出的 Gemini 4 Argon，Carbon 能够在复杂任务中投入更多推理 Token，进行假设探索、结果验证和边缘情况检查，更适合多步骤编码、复杂调试以及开放式科学研究。 在开发者工具方面，Gemini 4 Carbon 已通过 Gemini API 和 Google AI Studio 向付费开发者开放，同时面向企业客户提供服务。模型也正在向 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户逐步开放，覆盖 Google Antigravity、Gemini 应用和 Google

title: 中国汽车市场，不止一种赢法 | 极客车间
summary: 对消费者来说，当下的中国汽车消费市场，新品琳琅满目、供给充沛到足以挑花眼。 锚定一个预算区间，从外观设计、内饰风格，到舒适配置、智能化能力，总能找到各有所长的产品。选择足够丰富，也让一个问题变得更值得讨论：参数和价格之外，我们究竟为什么选择一辆车？ 从产品定义的角度看，造车很像求解一道「方程式」：在一定的成本和技术条件下，通过一系列判断、决策与取舍，找到品牌个性与用户需求的交点。 理解这些取舍背后的思考，也许能为我们评价一辆车提供另一个视角。 2026 年，基于全新纯电架构的全新梅赛德斯-奔驰纯电 GLC 正式上市。在这家百年车企眼中，「电车」本质上首先得是一辆拥有优秀底盘素质的「好车」，然后再往里加入电动化和智能化的相关能力。 所以，在这辆 30 万级的新车上，后轮转向让低速转弯更灵活，也让高速行驶更稳健； 电动两挡 变速箱和四驱断开装置，则兼顾了动力表现与能耗效率。保留鲜明奔驰设计语言的同时，纯电 GLC 也交出了超过 700 公里的 CLTC 续航成绩。 更让我们惊喜的，是它在智能化上的表现。深度体验搭载 Momenta R7 世界模型的辅助驾驶版本后，我最直接的感受是：车辆对路况的处理更自然，驾驶节奏也更容易让人理解。过去开启辅助驾驶，我常有一种「监督机器开车」的紧绷感；这一次，它在不少时刻让我想起坐在一位熟练司机身旁的从容。 所以我们也更能理解，一辆车的吸引力，既来自参数和价格，也藏在日常使用的细节里。那些产品定义时的判断与取舍，最终都会变成我们对一辆车的真实感受。 其实，挑选产品的过程，就是我们和产品背后的创新者们品味共振的过程。 *头图来源：极客公园

title: 千问办公押注 Team Agent，企业 AI 的流水线时刻真的来了
summary: 作者｜Cynthia 编辑｜郑玄 传说，光明之神巴德尔梦见自己将死，于是，巴德尔的母亲弗丽嘉遍走世间，令万物立下了绝不伤害他的誓言。众神也因此放下心来，甚至还发明了一种新的消遣：轮番向巴德尔投掷武器和石块，看着他毫发无损，来确定他们已经战胜了预言。直到一小枝被遗漏的槲寄生投向巴德尔。光明之神轰然倒下，诸神的黄昏由此拉开序章。 这是北欧神话中巴德尔之死的故事。危险早已被预见，人们也采取了行动，却仍然自欺欺人，把一次次看似成功的演示，当成了问题已经解决的证明 。 2026 年上半年的企业级 Agent 市场，也曾有过这样的笃定。 每一场发布会上，AI 写方案、做表格、敲代码、生成海报的单任务能力都会轮番刷新上限。台上演示环节的百发百中，带动台下掌声雷动， 所有人都觉得——企业级 AI 已经成熟了。 但年中效率复盘，所有人都尴尬地发现： 个人用 Agent 提效能翻三到十倍，落到整个团队、整个企业里，整体效率提升往往不到两倍 。一个人把报告写快十倍，并不能让另外三个部门提前给出确认。设计师更快做出了十套方案，运营可能还在等商家确认价格，仓库也还没有更新库存。单个员工的产出增加伴随的，是整个项目仍然要按照原来的方式往前推进。 11 月 9 日，千问办公 2.0 正式发布，直击这些痛点。 作为业内首个面向团队协作的「Team Agent」，千问办公 2.0 版本，把多人协作、文档共创和自动任务整合到同一个 Agent 产品中：团队可以关联原有工作群和资料，围绕同一个 Agent 持续讨论、分工和执行。Agent 可以实时理解项目信息，并和群成员协同工作，像项目经理一样推进项目和执行待办。 而伴随千问办公 2.0 打通生产级上下文， Agent 的 2.0 时代自此拉开序幕。 01 从单机到协作， Agent2.0 时代来了 如何弥合个体效率提升与组织效率提升之间的巨大鸿沟，是过去一年多企业级 Agent 市场最大的机遇所在。 围绕这个目标，主流探索大致分为两种：给 Agent 增加协作能力，以及给现有办公软件增加 Agent 能力。 多数 Agent 玩家的第一选择是第一种，给 Agent 加一个群聊。把同事拉进同一个 Agent 的项目组，大家一起讨论，AI 自然就有了团队上下文。 这个逻辑看上去顺理成章，但支持多人聊天，只是企业协作的起点。 工作群里为什么需要话题、已读、在线文档，甚至表情包？因为员工每天要在这里确认事情、表达态度、区分轻重缓急。一个被使用多年的工作群，还连接着客户、供应商和合作伙伴，积累着文件、会议与业务记录。 把几位同事邀请进新产品很容易，但让 Agent 获得完整的上下文却需要企业把完整工作流迁移过来。 甚至客户沟通、部门讨论、文档修改，最好都发生在这个新产品里。 你可以把同事拉进自己的 Agent，却很难要求客户先安装一个新的 AI 产品，才能向他发送优惠券。 对于企业来说，既有 IM 也远不只是聊天工具。人员关系、权限、审批和业务习惯，都已经形成。企业愿意为新能力付费，并不意味着它可以为新产品重新组织一遍所有人的工作。 也是因此，另一条路径选择反过来，给现有的 IM 工具加 Agent。这是更务实的选择，也确实走通了一多半 。 员工不用换地方，就在日常聊天的群里就能@机器人问问题、总结会议纪要、了解项目背景。 可问题在于，IM 终究是沟通场，不是生产场。群里的 Agent 最多能帮你整理聊天记录、提炼会议要点，真要写代码、做设计、改长文档、做复杂数据分析，还是得跳转到专门的生产工具里，上下文到这里也就断了。 讨论在群里，产出在别处，只要还需要员工下载文件、切换软件、重新介绍背景，协作成本就没有消失。 既然两条路都只走通了一半，那么为什么不将它们合二为一呢？ 千问办公 2.0 最先把这两种探索结合了起来。 一方面，它关联原有钉钉群和项目资料，让 Agent 了解业务正在发生什么；另一方面，它提供完整的任务执行和内容生产能力，让团队可以围绕同一个 Agent 继续做文档、处理表格、修改方案。 在企业版协作群里，不同岗位可以补充各自掌握的信息，Agent 小 Q 会据此整理进度、共识和问题，再按照团队确认的分工创建待办。有人接手项目，也能先了解当前安排，再继续自己的工作。 销售说过的话，可以成为方案同事产出的工作依据；方案发生的变化，也可以及时反映到交付安排中。团队不必等某个人收集好所有信息，再统一向 AI 下达指令。 Team Agent 也由此与个人 Agent 拉开了区别。 02 实测：AI 如何深度参与真实工作流 千问办公 2.0 发布后，我们第一时间进行了实测。 第一个场景选择了上下文足够复杂、需要做大量搬运工作的月底发票整理场景。 通常来说，报销时，员工会把电子发票发给财务，由财务整理、核对、分类，最后形成报销材料。清晰的流程背后，实际做起来却有许多琐碎的问题：同一张电子发票可能无意中被下载了两次、发送了两次。发票需要被分门别类管理，但不同项目、不同子公司抬头的费用，往往混在相同的上下文里。 每到月底，经常会出现几百张、上千张发票在同一时间被集中提交，完成审核、确认、整理这一套流程，专业财务也需要至少 1~2 天的时间。 于是，我自告奋勇给财务推荐了千问办公 2.0。在千问办公中，直接关联发票报销相关钉钉群，就完成了初步搭建。 接着，我只要一句话描述需求，并添加同事为协作者，千问办公就能自动解决剩下的所有问题。 过去需要一两天，把聊天记录里的文件逐一整理到文件夹，再上传给 AI 的流程，现在 Agent 可以直接自己从群聊中找到需要的内容，然后做汇总分析。 类似的工作在企业中还有很多。通常来说，这类任务本身并不复杂，但材料往往分散在不同人、不同项目中，上下文整合就需要花费大量的时间精力。 与之相对的，还有另一种情况——审批。 业务部门可能一天向法务发来 20 款合同，虽然法务只需要回复通过或者驳回，但判断的成本，可能一个合同就要花费半天的时间。 脑暴讨论也是如此。我们团队都有定期追踪行业论文的习惯，不同岗位的同事平时分别关注不同领域，大家会把看到的优质论文发在群里，再由专人汇总整理。这原本是一种很高效的办法，每个人替其他人筛选过一轮，整个团队就能快速掌握各个领域里最有价值的信息。 但随着人数和论文数量增加，对负责整合的同学来说，挨个通读、提炼要点就成了沉重的负担。 最终，我们选择把千问办公的协作空间关联到论文讨论日常群聊。每天新增了哪些论文、每篇论文的核心结论是什么、有哪些值得重点关注的创新点，Agent 全都可以自动梳理清楚。当然，总结群聊内容，产出 PPT，然后分配任务也不在话下。 阅读之后，还有讨论和修改。一些同事会用 PPT 来总结这一周的推荐论文。如果我觉得有问题，或者产生了新的想法，也可以在千问办公里直接与 AI 共同修改这个文档。过去，给 AI 改稿，需要先准确描述位置，再把结果复制回文档。多改几轮，还要核对版本。现在，借助人机共创模式，对话和文档可以被放在同一个窗口，选中需要调整的内容，提出要求，再检查原文中的修改。讨论和编辑围绕同一份文档进行，同事也能沿着这份成果继续工作。 此外，考虑到论文整理定期发生，我又把它设成了自动任务，在每周一和每周三定时执行。一次次重复交代的工作，逐渐变成了固定安排。 对我们这种小团队来说，千问办公 2.0 已经解决了大量上下文协作的时间。对那些组织更庞大、上下文更多的企业来说，深度协作带来的效果提升还会变得更加明显。银泰百货的直播卡券业务，就是最典型的样本。 在银泰，直播卡券业务覆盖全国 62 家品牌门店，联动 200 多名门店、商家与运营人员，年 GMV 超过 2 亿元。一张团购券从提报到最终上架，要经过档期确认、资料核对、内容制作、审核发布多个环节，仅需要核对的信息就有名称、价格、有效期、适用门店、素材等近 50 项。 过去，这些工作分散在几十个门店群里推进，没有任何一个群能看到完整的进度。运营人员要逐群翻聊天记录，把信息手动汇总到表格里，再通知下一环节的负责人跟进。大促期间一批卡券集中上线，整个团队要连轴转好几天，大部分精力都耗在了「找信息」和「同步进度」上。 内测千问办公 2.0 之后，事情开始变得不一样。 团队在千问办公里建起一个协作空间，把 60 多个门店钉钉群和卡券 AI 表格全部关联进去。门店的沟通方式没有任何变化，该在群里说什么还说什么，但所有的进度变化都会被 Agent 同步捕捉，自动更新到中央表格里。 负责人想知道一批卡券的准备情况，不用再逐群追问，直接在协作空间里提问，就能得到最新的整体进度。 此外，团队还设置了定时检查任务，Agent 会按固定时间梳理每张卡券的状态，列出已经满足上架条件的清单，再把资料不全、等待审批的事项整理成待办，推送给对应的负责人。 过去是人需要追着信息跑，现在信息和任务会主动找到人，生产协作的模式，开始随着企业级 Agent 的落地，逐渐发生变化。 03 为什么是千问办公？ 一个必须承认的事实是，千问办公能够把团队协作和专业 Agent 能力整合起来，原因 藏在阿里的业务基因里 。 钉钉连接着中国最大规模的企业客户，服务超 2000 万企业组织、近 8 亿用户。千问办公盘活了钉钉沉淀了十几年的企业上下文—— 消息、文档、审批、知识库，这些分散在业务流程里的海量数据，终于能完整、顺畅地喂给 Agent。 不止是钉钉，阿里云、电商平台也都是 2B 的服务。 对很多行业来说，生产创造是工作的主体，上下文搬运只是附加成本，忍一忍也能过去；但在电商与零售行业，运营、营销、客服、库存管理这类岗位，最终的产出可能只是一张报表、一个活动方案、一句客户回复，而九成以上的工作时间，都花在了收集信息、对齐信息、同步信息上。 上下文的摩擦力，是这类岗位每天都要面对的核心痛点。阿里本身就是全球最大的电商经济体之一，从淘宝天猫到银泰、菜鸟，内部有数百万从业者天天在这种痛点里打转。这种浸泡在真实业务里的体感，是纯 AI 实验室出身的团队，很难天然具备的。 最后，也是最容易被忽略的一点，是阿里滚雪球效应带来的更多行业 know how。 千问办公上线首月用户就突破 3000

title: The Jev Revolution: What Engineers Are Already Building with System One Models
summary: Today at the AI Engineer Code Summit , the main theme was system one models — non-generative models that return structured choices, scores, or probabilities. They’re also typically much faster and cheaper than reasoning LLMs (a.k.a. system two models). And who better to give an inspirational rallying cry for system one models than Diogo Almeida , co-founder and CEO of TypeSafe AI . Almeida was lead creator of Jev , the product that kicked off this trend less than two months ago. Jev was an instant revelation for AI engineers when it was released in September. In a podcast with Latent Space on launch (which quickly became our most popular episode of the year), Almeida explained the core problem with making LLMs the heart of software: reliability . In his keynote at AIE Code today, he took it a step further by claiming that Jev is “reliable intelligence” that should be used for “just automating everything.” Integrating system one models into code Of particular interest to AI engineers is Almeida’s point that system one models should become integrated with code. We’ve also seen new ways to work with agents. OpenAI’s workshop addressed all three, and I also had some followup questions on these topics for Kundel, after the session. title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
summary: Today’s podcast comes from a real life mystery: We are big fans of Cloudflare’s developer platform, and Cloudflare Email is a convenient tool especially when all your domains are already on Cloudflare. So why do agents keep suggesting we use Resend despite having an existing “home bias” and much larger incumbent player? Well, we got the guy who “does AEO for resend” - the CEO of AEO, Zeno Rocha, who has been writing about AEO since 2024 and Agent Experience since Feb 2025 , on the pod today: In a recent AEO study, Claude Code picked Resend first in 64 of the 102 email recommendations the researchers could extract. SendGrid came first seven times, yet showed up 55 times as an alternative. If the developer asks an agent to implement email and accepts the patch, how often does anyone get around to trying the second choice? The study breaks down the results by model and app. Our more recent comprehensive AEO study was a bit more competitive, with Postmark coming up top for most models. title: NaiveAI Promises 2,100 Tokens per Second. How Well Does It Code?
summary: Editor’s note: With this post, we are launching a new series focused on trying new models and products with unbiased reviews. Reach out with suggestions to tips@latent.space. Naive-N0.5-Flash is a new open-weights model built for AI coding tasks and tuned to generate as many tokens per second as possible . It was developed by a Chinese company called NaiveAI , with the aim of speeding up engineering and research workflows so that teams can experiment, iterate and solve complex problems faster. The model is an evolution of Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.5 , which NaiveAI has trained further for long-context reasoning and paired with its own NaiveRT inference engine. Naive-N0.5-Flash arrives with a bold pitch: a model built largely by AI and trained to do AI research itself, with recursive self-improvement as the long-term goal. To see what changed, it helps to know where it started. MiMo-V2.5 is a 310B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 15B active parameters, trained on 48T tokens. Its language backbone inherits the hybrid design of MiMo-V2-Flash, which mixes sliding-window attention (SWA) with global self-attention. NaiveAI's recipe starts from those weights. title: [AINews] Fable 5.2 retakes World #1 LLM spot as $ANT IPO roadshow begins

title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
summary: Claude Fable 5.2 pays close attention to who owns the code it works on. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model tended to add to the existing structure when the prompt said nothing about ownership or presented the code base as someone else’s, even when that duplicated existing code. When the prompt said the code base was the model’s own, it often consolidated duplicated code and sometimes made related fixes without being asked. If you want the model to improve the structure as it works, say that the code is its own: You are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you. The ownership sentence makes the model much more likely to consolidate duplicated code into one shared function. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model consolidated duplicated code in under 10 percent of runs without the sentence and in about 75 percent of runs with it. — Prompting Claude Fable 5.2 , Anthropic documentation Tags: prompt-engineering , anthropic , generative-ai , ai , llms , claude-mythos-fable

But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal. title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
summary: The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game. This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance "declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity." Noting "a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools," the group of jurors called out AI's ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still "not a foregone conclusion in our industry." title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
summary: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities. summary: Amazon is betting that many Ring customers will also want an AI-powered security drone and robot patrolling their homes or offices. But the company’s upcoming Ring Robotic products are also certain to intensify privacy concerns previously raised around a prior Amazon attempt to popularize a flying security camera. The Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam are expected to reach customers starting at the end of 2026 and in early 2027, respectively, according to an Amazon announcement posted on November 10. Amazon describes the devices as relying on an AI Pilot system that uses each device’s cameras along with “specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing” to plan patrol routes while autonomously navigating around obstacles such as furniture. Both devices also use that AI Pilot system to digitally map the floor plan of the customer’s home or business. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it. You had one job Research from security firm Claroc shows that the exposed data includes things like internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results, galley checklists from a celebrity cruise line, and employee names and ID numbers. Ironically, some of the sensitive data comes from two-dozen apps built by SpaceXSI (the name of the now-merged SpaceX and xAI) itself. title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
summary: Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called "big math" is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend. Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. In 2005, Strogatz extended his study of synchronicity to the crowds that caused the wobbling of London's Millennium Bridge . summary: Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. DeepMind's physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There's the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that's Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5. DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. summary: Impervious to battlefield jamming, drones physically connected to human operators by miles of fiber-optic cables have become such a common weapon of war in Ukraine that trees and fields are strewn with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. But importing such fiber-optic material from China has become more costly as drone warfare’s needs compete with global demand from AI data centers for the same limited supply—and so Ukrainian drone makers have been adapting. Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, the Ukrainians have been forced out of necessity to continually develop battlefield innovations involving first-person view (FPV) quadcopter drones and other heavier types of drones. But it was the Russian military that first deployed unjammable fiber-optic drones to repel Ukrainian forces’ cross-border incursion into the Kursk Oblast in 2024. The Ukrainians quickly followed suit in developing their own fiber-optic drones, given the drones’ capability to shrug off electronic warfare jamming that could neutralize radio-controlled drones. Russia and Ukraine have relied on Chinese suppliers for some off-the-shelf drones and a wide array of drone components, including bulk orders of fiber wound around very large spools or sometimes small finished spools ready for installation on drones. summary: By Yakov Filippenko One day, I woke up to a notice that our app had been removed from Apple’s App Store. For the next month or so, we racked our brains trying to find out why. We even reached out to our internal contacts, only for them to tell us that helping us could put their jobs at risk. Nothing seemed to work. For years, the App Store’s unwritten contract seemed simple. As long as you followed the guidelines, your storefront would remain available. Then a removal notice arrives, and you wonder whether your business can survive. In 2025, Apple removed 166,899 apps and reported just 423 restorations after appeals. As we learned, being caught in it feels like watching your business collapse, with no guarantee of recovery. It’s not all bad news, though. We survived, and this episode taught me that platform dependency is ultimately infrastructure risk. As founders, we prepare for cloud outages and payment failures, but losing access to the platform that brings us customers deserves the same attention. title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
summary: Macronutrients don’t have popularity contests. But if they did, protein would surely be this era’s winner. For everything from sodas to snack bars to pasta, it’s now standard practice for food and drink makers to play up protein content whenever feasible. While we may cut carbs and fret over fat, most of us are still keen on protein. Startups and their backers have been riding this trend too. Over the past decade, investors have poured billions into upstarts promising cheaper, tastier and more sustainable ways to meet our protein quotas. Unfortunately, many of their earlier bets have fared poorly. Vast sums poured into lab-grown meat several years ago, for instance, have so far failed to produce a success story. Former high-flying plant-based meat startups Beyond (now public) and Impossible Foods have seen their valuations wither. Others have shuttered. In response, more recent startup investment has shifted away from meat substitutes and toward stuffing more protein into other packaged foods and drinks. It’s a fad that’s obvious on supermarket shelves, where startups and established brands alike relentlessly tout the added protein in their noodles, pancakes, cereals, energy bars, popcorn and so on. summary: Anthropic is seeking to secure up to $88.5 billion in its planned IPO and a concurrent private placement, potentially making it the largest-ever fundraise tied to a public market debut. summary: A total of 34 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in October, adding more than $96 billion in value and $14.8 billion in total funding to the board. title: Startup Founders Are Using AI To File Patents. Here’s Where DIY Becomes A Liability.
summary: By Michael Drapkin and Nathan Mutter Patents can help startups establish competitive advantage, attract investors and protect innovations. But the traditional patent process is expensive, slow and difficult to navigate, particularly for companies with limited resources. Michael Drapkin, founding partner of Landfall IP. AI is changing that equation. General-purpose tools can research existing patents, document inventions and generate drafts that look like patent applications in minutes. Handling the process themselves can seem like an easy way for founders to save money. But AI’s capabilities are jagged. AI can perform some tasks remarkably well while missing legal and strategic issues that determine a patent’s commercial value. An application can look sophisticated while providing little meaningful protection. For example, a patent’s claims define its legal boundaries and what you can stop competitors from doing. Mistakes involving claim scope may remain hidden until an investor, acquirer or competitor scrutinizes the company’s intellectual property. Nathan Mutter, managing partner and founder of Landfall IP. The question isn’t whether startups should use AI. It’s how much founders can safely do themselves and when legal expertise becomes essential. Who are you and what business did you start? Hello, this is Vishal Goswami, an eCommerce consultant and founder of Friction Studio , a Shopify Agency. At Friction Studio, we believe in making commerce better for everyone. That is, we help you sell in a frictionless manner. Through our years of experience and expertise, we help DTC brands design, build and grow their store on Shopify. We help them build a brand presence and grow exponentially by working on the right strategies and creating conversion-focused Shopify stores with a functional user experience. As said above, we are a team of Shopify experts focused on removing the friction between eCommerce design, development, and strategy to enable DTC growth. This venture of Friction Studio has been a roller coaster ride. It reminds me how back in the days, I had started this agency with just $100, and we are making $10k/month on average today. It feels excellent to cater to big brands in the industry and onboard Shopify plus merchants. Today, I feel privileged to be creating a significant impact in the eCommerce ecosystem and helping merchants ease their selling journey. What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? I wasn t always a Shopify expert until I had to become one! As any other Indian kid, I have had the same routine: school, homework, eat, sleep, and repeat. However, my eternal interest and love for computers have brought me here. At 17, I learned HTML, CSS, and Javascript all by myself. Back then, I was working on WordPress for some local clients. However, one day I came across dropshipping and Shopify. I then kicked off my Shopify journey by starting a dropshipping store. As always, I had this forever interest in website designing and development, so I designed one for myself and posted it in a Facebook group full of brand owners. I got to see there was a lot of traction on my post, which also led me to my first client from that. Thanks to my forever passion for trying new things, I started designing and developing Shopify stores for small brands. When I started all this in 2016, the times were tough, and I could not even afford a laptop on my own. I recall when I was issued a laptop during my high school from the government’s side for being a scholar. I used to learn everything from coding to designing from the free tutorials available on the internet. After creating few stores I started an agency with my partner and built it from scratch to become Official Shopify Experts. Later I left the agency I built with my partner due to some reasons in late 2020. Then I started thinking about creating a new one from scratch with a strong and unique vision. That s when it all began. I began learning the ropes of branding and aligning design with it for myself and later for brands struggling with it. In December 2020, I finally took the call of taking everything I had learned so far. I started with setting up stores for D2C brands under the name of Friction Studio. We wanted to make the experience of taking your brand online frictionless so that businesses don’t have to spend weeks and months building a great store that converts. As I got into the eCommerce industry, I saw brands struggling to find someone who could understand their vision and help them translate it into an impressive storefront. Since that day, Friction Studio has delivered optimized design solutions to brands of all sizes. We optimize, redefine, and provide you with a custom-made Shopify storefront based on your niche. I saw a gap in relating the goals and vision of the brands. Either their understanding of the store setup was not up to the mark, or it resulted in a website that did not represent their brand s message. Their websites lacked the functionalities which could turn visitors into customers. Let alone even create a lasting impression on these visitors! Creating an impactful Shopify website is challenging, with best practices constantly evolving. However, with Friction Studio design and Shopify experts guiding the way, brands enjoyed exceptional conversion rates. I had this mindset of fueling the business growth of various brands through commercially-optimized website designs. We took matters into our hands from brand strategy, design, and custom implementation while setting up an online store. We worked closely with D2C businesses over the next few months. It started as a learning curve and resulted in what you know as the Friction Studio today! Back then, my finances didn t look great. I barely had some $100-200 to invest. I had to start it all from scratch as I had zero clients that time. Take us through the process of designing your services. I started working with Shopify store owners from various community and Facebook groups. I worked on the design and development front by taking help from some experienced designers in the industry and exploring new design trends per various niches and products. The first few clients were from Facebook groups. I had built certain valuable connections by answering queries and generating value in groups and communities. Later I saw we needed to specify some niches and break down our services and offerings. Looking at my previous clientele, I derived that we were good at building stores for supplements, fitness, health wellness, CBD, skincare, and lifestyle brands mainly. I needed to set our work process to develop the best results for brands and provide them with the best experience. So I made a small team of freelancers and made SOPs for them. This included a concrete system for our sales, onboarding clients, discovery sessions, and service delivery. We focused more on brand targeting, needs, story, goals, and vision. I developed a foolproof process to understand their vision, mission, and goal. The first person to join me was my closest friend - Devang Tiwari. He is a man with excellent management skills. He reduced my workload, and I knew my business was in safe hands right after I handed him specific responsibilities. He is good at crises and can manage things even at the last minute. He has always been with me in every stage of building Friction Studio. Do not ever come out without a plan and clear vision. Otherwise, you will end up spinning in a fixed cycle without any goals. I further made a full-service breakdown and optimized delivering the best service. Building the right team was one of the biggest challenges for me. Finding people with the same vision and goals as yours is always hard. However, after spending numerous hours and energy, I found some good people who could join us and improve the quality. In those days, I used to work 15 hours a day. I handled everything by myself, from making work, communication, client updates, sales, and everything you can think of in a startup. This picture of early days in January, me learning systems and management so I can handle the projects in a better way. Describe the process of launching the business. Friction Studio has been a dream project! Seeing everything turn into reality kept giving me goosebumps. To say I had everything planned from day one will not do justice. Instead, I kept proceeding steadily, and every next step has been a discovery for me. My friend helped me decide the name of our venture as Friction Studio while we were just chit-chatting about websites and services. Initially, our major focus for marketing was content marketing and SEO. We started with Instagram, Facebook, Linkedin, and website marketing. My Airtable Plugin Grew 4X To $23K/Mo (2024) ➜ Hello! Who are you and what business did you start? Hi! My name is Andy Cloke and I am the founder of Data Fetcher . Data Fetcher is a way to import data from anywhere into Airtable . For anyone that hasn’t heard of Airtable, it’s basically Google Sheets on steroids. It lets you visualize and manage your data in amazing ways, but sometimes it’s hard to get the data you need into it in the first place. That’s where Data Fetcher comes in! My customers are all Airtable users but their use cases are very varied. Many are importing financial (stock prices, exchange rates) data, cryptocurrency prices, or marketing (e.g. Google Analytics) metrics. I also have a customer connecting to a vineyard CRM and another importing sewing patterns from a sewing social network called Ravelry ! People have connected to over 1000 different applications using Data Fetcher. The way my friend described it recently was ‘the long tail is much longer than you think’. Just over a year after launching, Data Fetcher has reached 190 paying customers and $6500 in MRR. I’m really happy with this consistent growth and it seems to be speeding up! The app has also become a critical part of many businesses’ operations around the world. Revenue growth since launch in November 2020 What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? I studied engineering at university but never loved it, so after graduating I taught myself to code to get a career in software. I liked the idea of building my own projects and being able to work from anywhere. Whilst learning to code, I launched Verbly , a way to learn Spanish verb conjugations. It got to the front page of Hacker News and lots of people were using it! The dopamine hit of lots of people using something I built in my bedroom is something I’ve been fairly obsessed with ever since. I worked for a few startups as a freelance software (JavaScript React.js) developer and launched more projects on the side. The first one to make any money was Influence Grid , a directory of TikTok influencers. I bootstrapped it to $3k MRR and then sold the app to another company for $55k. This was the first time one of my projects had made real money and it felt like massive validation of all the evenings/ weekends I was spending on my side projects. I follow a simple framework for coming up with business ideas, explained in this Tweet . Basically, you find a new platform that is growing massively, look at existing successful tools for more mature platforms and build an equivalent tool for the new platform. I noticed a Google Sheets add-on called API Connector and built the equivalent for Airtable. I did not copy API Connector mindlessly, as there are big differences between Sheets and Airtable, but the core app idea came from following this. I also gave credit to the founder of API connector when I launched. We now have a great working relationship and she has even copied Data Fetcher features into API Connector. After getting the first few Data Fetcher customers, I knew this was an idea I wanted to work on for the next few years. Looking at other app marketplaces, e.g. Shopify Slack, it’s possible to bootstrap an app to life-changing revenue as a solo founder. That is the goal I’m working towards now. Take us through the process of designing, prototyping, and manufacturing your first product. The timing of my idea for Data Fetcher was fortunate, as Airtable had just opened up their app marketplace to third-party developers. Airtable apps also use a technology (React.js) I had lots of experience with. I spent a month developing the first version of the app, and another three months getting it through Airtable’s app marketplace review process. The first version of the app was pretty terrible, but it had the core functionality of being able to connect to an API. The Airtable app marketplace does not yet have a way to charge users for your app, so I had to build this myself. Although it was rudimentary, it was enough to get a few paying customers and know I was onto something! I then started working through the backlog of essential features. I also started getting user requests for features and adding these to the product too. Airtable apps are released like mobile apps, where you must submit to the app marketplace and wait for the approval. This means it’s hard to push quick fixes/ updates. Therefore I spent lots of time thoroughly testing every version of the app before release and making sure it did not break things for existing users. I also wrote a thorough Help Center with guides to all the features, to reduce the support after I launched. Describe the process of launching the business. There were minimal startup costs for the app. I did all the software development myself, so the main investment was simply my time. I had the funds from selling Influence Grid, which I used to live off and pay for a few things like the domain (from Namecheap ) and Heroku servers. As I developed the app, I tweeted about what I was building and sent people who were interested in Twitter to a landing page, where I collected their emails. When the app went live, I emailed these people and posted on some Airtable social media groups/ forums. This helped drive some initial awareness and customers within the first two weeks. Shortly after that, I launched Data Fetcher on Product Hunt , which drove more customers. The biggest lesson here was being patient. I also had to trust my gut that the app would attract customers and my hard work would be worth it. It took 3 months to get the app through Airtable’s app review process as the marketplace was so new at the time. There wasn’t much I could do to speed this up, so I had to sit tight. Since launch, what has worked to attract and retain customers? One thing that’s really helped is how early I was in the Airtable app marketplace and the relative lack of competition. Around 70-80% of my customers simply discover the app through the marketplace. I’ve focused on improving the app marketplace listing with testimonials, clear feature descriptions, and links to helpful resources. The fact that Data Fetcher has a freemium pricing model has really helped me get the most out of the marketplace channel. Users can install and try it for free and only pay once they reach certain usage limits. A healthy 10% of my free users convert to paying customers. People use the fact that ‘Freemium is a marketing strategy, not a revenue model’ as a way to bash freemium. But if it’s done correctly and you are aware of the risks (e.g. increased server costs and support), it can be very powerful. One thing that has really helped is looking at where most of my customers are already coming from and reducing friction in this funnel. There will definitely be more competition in the marketplace soon, so I’m working on developing other marketing channels. I’ve focused on content marketing, by creating Data Fetcher’s no-code blog and YouTube channel . The content is fairly simple. Each video/ blog post shows how to use Data Fetcher to do a certain task, e.g. import stock prices to Airtable , but it works very well! About 20% of my customers are now coming through these channels. I want to scale up this content marketing soon and start publishing content more consistently. How Two College Roommates Started An Online CBD Business (2019) ➜ This is a follow up story for Plain Jane. If you're interested in reading how they got started, published almost 8 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. I’m Lindsey Holthaus and I co-founded Plain Jane in 2018 with Evan Marshall. We’re a CBD brand based in Ashland Oregon. Many people are now familiar with hemp-derived CBD products due to the rapid explosion in CBD products. We manufacture and sell CBD hemp flower-based products including joints, cigarettes, flowers in jars, kief, moon rocks, and many more. Our first update was in 2018 when we 10xd our revenue in one year. By 2020 we doubled again in size to nearly 500K a month. We decided in 2020, we should either take on investors or make a successful exit. After exploring our options we decided to sell the brand after 2 years in business. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? In our last update in 2019 we had 10xed our revenue in year 1 and we were at 250K a month in sales. By 2020 we had doubled that. Part of this was circumstantial. The pandemic had shut down most smoke shops and consumers moved more to online retailers. At the same time, we had a product that may help people feel more relaxed which many people desperately needed during such a chaotic time. Luckily we had already built a trusted brand by this time and had strong SEO when people went to search online. Know when to keep going and when to let go. Up until that point, we continued to put our energy and money into methods that helped build brand awareness and increase traffic. Here are the strategies we used to build a strong, authentic brand. SEO: We’ve continued to improve in ranking for many industry-specific keywords. We’ve done this through both link building and organic traffic as traditional marketing routes are still a no-go for cannabis companies. News articles have been helpful for more organic traffic but they are harder to come by. Some tools I like to use for SEO are AHREFS, similar web, and Semrush. Social Media: Instead of paying big celebrities to market our products we’ve used hundreds of micro “canna influencers” which are more affordable and more effective. The few times we played our hand with bigger-name celebrity influencers, the ROI was never worth it. We have built a solid following on our instagram and use that to market new products and build brand authenticity through social justice-focused posts thrown in. Customer Satisfaction: You can have the best SEO in the world but if your product sucks then you won’t have returning customers. In a competitive field like ours, you can’t afford to be less than perfect. We work hard on building product lines around what consumers want. We’ve started adding topicals, edibles, and vapes as the flower market has become more competitive. We offer free samples to anyone interested in the product because we know the product can sell itself. I use Klaviyo for email campaigns and flows to keep engagement and conversion rates high. We manufacture almost all of our products in-house to keep a close eye on quality and have fewer supply issues. We use Zendesk for customer service and we use Trustpilot to monitor customer reviews and stay on top of any issues. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? Starting (and selling) a business has taught me so much more than any University ever could. I feel like I am constantly learning lessons. Here are a few of the biggest lessons I’ve learned: Nothing is certain: 2020 was an intense year. We were dealing with a pandemic which on one hand helped our eCommerce business but on the other hand hurt fulfillment because of the labor shortage. On top of a pandemic, a few weeks before the sale was finalized, a huge fire ripped through our town in Southern Oregon, destroying the homes and all the belongings of multiple employees. The fire was half a mile away from our production facility. In just a few minutes, everything we had worked so hard for could have been gone (yes we had insurance, which leads me to say: always have insurance). The laws are also constantly changing, at times conflicting, and difficult to keep up with. Wreckage from the fires Learn from Your Mistakes (fast): Have we made mistakes? Absolutely. We’ve switched our backend platform quite a few times to save money. The amount of money saved was never worth the headache of glitches on new platforms. I’ve personally taken too long to let people go instead of trusting my intuition as soon as I felt it. We started growing and realized after the first harvest that financially it didn’t make sense for us so after the first year we stopped. There are always going to be mistakes but learning quickly and not making the same ones twice is the important thing. Patience: Running a business can be tough. The more you grow, the more tiny decisions that constantly need to be made. When we first started, we were small and there were only so many things that could be done. Now the work is never-ending, there is constantly something I could be doing to make the company better. Knowing that it never ends, I’ve had to learn patience with myself and with employees so that I can sustain it. What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? For the business, I think the plan is to continue as is but to focus on international expansion and gaining a larger foothold in edible and topicals. Evan is no longer with us but he’s working on some of his new projects for fun. I don’t necessarily have a 5-year plan, I take everything a few months at a time. I enjoy being creative and problem-solving so definitely in the next few years I’ll be coming up with my next business idea. Have you read any good books in the last year? Parable of the Sower- Octavia Butler We Speak for Ourselves - D. Watkins The Plague - Camu (timely) Behind the Beautiful Forevers - Katherine Boo The Shame of the Prisons - Ben Bagdikian War Against All Puerto Ricans - N. Denis Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? Know when to keep going and when to let go. We got lucky in that we were in a fast-growing market. Our sales picked up relatively early and we broke even early on (because we had to). Unless you’re heavy in R D or a genuine tech startup, if your burn rate is increasing and you’re a year or more into the business you might want to consider a different route. With that being said, you can’t expect to make money right away, at least give yourself the 6 months to a year if you can afford it. The other important thing is to know the economics of your company. Understand your COGS and how your pricing fits into the goal of the company (whether solely e-commerce or both e-commerce and brick and mortar). Let the data drive your decision-making. Know how much it costs to acquire each customer and their ltv. Not having a good grasp of your spending and wasting money can be the reason a potentially viable company fails. We took a few risks with money but always for just a few months and then reevaluated if it was worth it. Don’t make the mistake of hiring too many people too fast. When we started, the two of us were doing nearly everything from fulfillment to customer service.

If you're interested in reading how they got started, published almost 6 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. I am Sunny Choudhary, a 25-year-old co-founder of PortraitFlip with a B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering from Vellore Institute of Technology, Chennai. For three years PortraitFlip e-commerce has been serving as the bridge between artists and customers who need Handmade Portraits. We deliver handmade portraits globally with a major clientele being the USA. We provide all types of medium for portraits from Charcoal, Oil, Acrylic, Pencil, Color Pencil, and Watercolor. Interestingly, we never thought of making this big. It all started as a college side hustle because we needed money to fulfill our whims and fancies. When you covered us last year, the company was yielding 3.5crs with capital of merely Rs. 23,000. Today, after three years of launch, PortraitFlip has a turnover of 8crs. We have seen a growth of 60% in the last year. What makes PortraitFlip stand out even today is our 100% customer satisfaction guarantee. We not only provide free shipping worldwide but we also give our customers the privilege of getting unlimited revisions of their painting and provide them with a 100% money-back guarantee. We make sure to choose the best artists across the world so that there are no doubts in the hearts of our customers. PortraitFlip firmly believes that the customer is the King and to get the best sales, it is important to provide the best service. Quality is our priority and a hassle-free customer experience is the driving factor. Funding is not always an option but bootstrapping is. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? The business, in terms of revenue, has definitely made a bigger space. Since most of our traffic comes from organic marketing, we decided to have a team of digital marketing strategists work on the website front. One aspect that we were lacking from the beginning was our Social Media Marketing which took a boom this year. Instagram and Pinterest were the two most growing platforms that got in traffic. Social Media is a GenZ concept and as difficult to understand as the generation itself. But we also realized that the only person that could do this the best was a GenZ. And so happened. We hired a social media strategist who worked diligently on growing our social presence and creating a brand name on platforms like Instagram and Pinterest. From nothing, to getting a considerable amount of website traffic, this is how our social media gain looks like. We are also trying to make space for our brand on Tiktok. However, that has been one of the biggest challenges for us. Art market has a lot of influence on Tiktok and while we knew that we could have made it big there, we hail from India. TikTok is clearly banned here and so became our idea of expanding on TikTok. But, like I always say “Outsourcing is the Key”, we outsourced TikTok Marketing to a Social Media Marketing agency in the USA. Voila! We are now slowly progressing towards a better reach on TikTok as well. Any startup is a series of ups and downs. You either learn from it or give up completely. I would not say that PortraitFlip did not face any setbacks since last year but it is a part of growing. Our traffic saw a considerable decline this year and we had to rely on Ads. However, other things like Instagram and Email marketing worked out for us. We practiced Email marketing the entire year and I can say that we generated 20% of our sales this year through Email Marketing. Instagram stories have also brought in traffic. We often forget that Social Media, although a marketing platform, is a great customer service tool as well. If catered with the right responses, you can generate a decent sale from Social platforms in spite of not having a shop on it. Which brings me to the point of keeping existing customers happy. The Gifting industry does not give you a lot of scope to retain customers but it does give a lot of space to acquire new customers. PortraitFlip’s mantra is to keep your customers happy. Your customers are never wrong. Even if they are, they still deserve to be treated in a way that keeps them happy. As long as your customers are jubilant, you keep generating sales. One of the biggest challenges right now is our wavering traffic. It is getting a little difficult to understand exactly what is hitting our website but we are constantly trying to make the user experience of our website more user friendly. The in-house team is trying to make things work and we are assertive that this year we will see an increase in organic traffic again. You are not an expert in everything. Outsourcing can make a lot of things simple for you. By the time you learn and implement something, the time will be gone. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? PortraitFlip has learnt the biggest lessons by making mistakes and we as a team are never scared of making mistakes. One of them was the idea of shifting from WordPress to PHP. Our biggest dream has always been to create an aesthetically pleasing and hassle-free Order Flow through PHP. With that thought, we decided to hire a set of highly skilled website developers and put in a lot of resources to make the team strong. Unfortunately, it did not work out for us. It was saddening that all the efforts and resources went in vain. It can be counted as a poor decision on our part but that did lead to one good thing. We are revamping our Order Flow through WordPress and are trying to achieve a similar appearance. Which also takes me to another very careless mistake we fell prey to and is worth mentioning. The making changes to the order process of our website occurred to us in the month of July, 2021. Without thinking twice, we started burning our midnight oil towards making designs and layouts for the website. By the time we could finish off the work, time was already hitting our peak season. Tampering with the website during peak felt risky and totally not worth it. And so, once again, we had to put the website changes aside and focus on catering the needs of our customers.
